No. `u.launch()` fails: 'u' is of type 'unknown'. `a.launch()` compiles (and would crash at run time); inside the typeof check, u is a string.

Why: any turns checking off; unknown keeps it on and asks you to prove the type first.

Docs: TypeScript Handbook — More on Functions — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/functions.html#unknown
quote: This is similar to the any type, but is safer because it's not legal to do anything with an unknown value:

title: Fix lengthOf(value: unknown)
quote: This analysis of code based on reachability is called control flow analysis, and TypeScript uses this flow analysis to narrow types as it encounters type guards and assignments.
